#### 1. infantile-onset ascending hereditary spastic paralysis  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.794)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-8876198, Reactome:R-HSA-9013149)

Loss-of-function mutations in ALS2 disrupt Rab5-mediated endosomal trafficking, which is crucial for neuronal health. This disruption leads to motor neuron degeneration and progressive muscle weakness, manifesting as spasticity in both diseases.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in ALS2 that are exclusively associated with one disease and not the other, or demonstration of distinct functional consequences of ALS2 mutations in each disease context, would falsify this hypothesis. Furthermore, if mutations in ALS2 were shown to be completely absent in one of the diseases, this hypothesis would be refuted. _(variant: rs113553382)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of ALS2 in both diseases could lead to the development of therapies targeting the common downstream pathways, such as endosomal trafficking, which might benefit patients with either amyotrophic lateral sclerosis type 2, juvenile or infantile-onset ascending hereditary spastic paralysis.
